name: Cosmetic tourism to Korea

card.summary: Cosmetic tourism to Korea means travelling to South Korea for plastic surgery, dermatology and skincare treatments to change one's appearance.
card.note: Procedures abroad involve the usual surgical risks plus follow-up and broker issues; Korean law regulates brokers and requires malpractice insurance for registered institutions.

quick.overview:
South Korea has become a destination where overseas patients book cosmetic surgery, dermatology and skin treatments. For people trying to improve their looks, it offers access to a large cosmetic-medicine sector, with procedures from eyelid and nose surgery to skin clinic treatments.

Government data summarized in public sources show a rapid growth of foreign patients over the 2010s, with cosmetic-purpose visits making up a large share. The state promoted the sector through a national medical tourism brand and set up support centres.
quick.how: Visitors typically choose a clinic, often through a registered agency or an online platform, travel for consultation and the procedure, and arrange recovery time before returning home. Skincare shopping and dermatology treatments are commonly combined with trips. Registered medical institutions are subject to rules on insurance and brokering.
quick.risks: Surgery abroad carries the same risks as at home, with the added matter of aftercare once the patient has flown back. South Korean rules penalize unregistered brokers, and registered institutions must carry malpractice liability insurance.

lead: Cosmetic tourism to Korea is travel to South Korea for procedures intended to change appearance, including cosmetic surgery, dermatology treatments and skincare. [1] It belongs to the broader field of medical tourism in South Korea, which the government began promoting as a destination in 2009 under a national brand, Medical Korea. [1]

For someone looking to improve their looks, the appeal is the density of clinics and the range of procedures. Foreign patient numbers rose from about 60,000 in 2009 to a cumulative 2.76 million by 2019, according to a Wikipedia summary of government statistics, and cosmetic-purpose visits reached 464,452 in 2018, up 16.7% from 2017. [1]

South Korea was cited in a 2014 ISAPS survey as having the highest per-capita rate of cosmetic surgery in the world. [1] The largest source countries of patients are China, Japan, the United States, Russia and Mongolia. [1]

chain: Receive cosmetic surgery or dermatology treatment
angle.text: People travel to Korea to have surgical and skin procedures performed there. The results come from the procedure itself; the trip is the means of access.

infobox: Broker penalties, malpractice insurance since 2016, VAT refund on cosmetic procedures [1]

paras: The Korea Health Industry Development Institute launched Medical Korea in 2009, and a 2016 act supported international patient attraction and overseas expansion. A 10% VAT refund for cosmetic procedures was set up in 2016 and extended to the end of 2022. Medical tourism centres opened at Incheon Airport in December 2018 and in Seoul in February 2021. [1]

Unregistered brokers or hospitals can face up to three years in prison and a fine of 30 million won, and registered institutions have been required to carry malpractice insurance since 2016. A hospital accreditation programme evaluates institutions against a standards list. [1] The summary source itself notes that its coverage is promotional in tone.

timeline.event: Act supporting international patients; VAT refund for cosmetic procedures; insurance requirement. [1]
Cosmetic-purpose visits reach 464,452; Incheon airport centre opens. [1]
